skill.authRuleApplicability: This backend uses its validated Play Cookie session, issued after verified SSO identity proof; the Web SDK getSession/getUser route-guard API distinction does not replace this server-side session validator.

evidence: http/api.ts:386-407 validates multiplayer gate, exact allowed Origin and Play Cookie session before reading the operation key and calling createRoom.
http/api.ts:483-489 requires sessions.validate(cookie); auth/session.ts validates hashed opaque sessions and expiry. The operation key alone grants no authority.

room/service.ts:94-131 validates UUID v4, derives a stable SHA256 room ID from namespace, authenticated UID and normalized key, and stores the immutable original creator UID and canonical game/rules/version/capacity fingerprint.
Changed payload returns IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; a different UID has a different room ID. Expired recorded operations return ROOM_EXPIRED rather than allocating another room.
room/cloudbase-repository.ts:36-48 reads the same room document within runTransaction and refuses an existing document before writing the room and initial members in that transaction.

room/service.ts:110-125 uses the persistent room fact before its process-local in-flight Map; :186-195 re-reads authoritative storage after a create error, including a late/lost commit acknowledgement.
The process-local Map is an optimization, not the durable source of idempotency. Service recreation can recover the stored fact without a new collection.
creationRequest is only an optional private stored room field validated by storage-schema.ts:110-113.
HTTP room creation uses createRoomSnapshot; current and legacy room snapshots explicitly list public fields and omit creationRequest.
colyseus/play-room.ts:494-499 updates only roomId/revision/status/gameId in replicated state; :721-730 sends explicit room/game snapshots, not aggregate serialization.
No full request headers, environment, context or x-cloudbase-context are returned or logged in the reviewed paths.

HTTP logs list requestId/method/path/status/errorCode/duration only; generic database failures map to a fixed INTERNAL_ERROR message. Health reports explicit flags and booleans rather than configured secrets.

installedSdkVerification.method: Read installed SDK source and declarations only; no initialization or network calls.
installedSdkVerification.transactionApi: The actual Db imports transaction/index. dist/commonjs/transaction/index.js:66-76 passes the transaction to the callback, awaits commit, and returns callbackRes directly; :82-102 rolls back and throws other errors, retrying only DATABASE_TRANSACTION_CONFLICT.
installedSdkVerification.getApi: dist/commonjs/document.js:169-196 returns transaction data as one document or null; ordinary document reads return an array. firstRecord supports both shapes and treats a missing transactional document as absent.
installedSdkVerification.setApi: Document.set receives the document object directly, not a {data:...} wrapper. Its request uses merge:false, upsert:true and transactionId. Awaited SDK errors reject the transaction.
installedSdkVerification.errorHandling: The Node SDK defaults throwOnCode=true; utils and tcbapirequester convert returned service codes into thrown errors. The project does not disable this behavior.
installedSdkVerification.conclusion: Reviewed create/get/set and transaction result handling match the installed SDK. The serial adapter fixture uses the ordinary-array get shape, which the same parser supports; it is not a live transaction test.

existingEvidence.scope: Existing report records 55 local server regressions including seven new creation/idempotency cases; parent also reported 31 complete room tests. This review did not rerun them.
reviewedCases: discarded successful HTTP response then retry
service recreation over serialized room facts
different UID and changed payload conflict
repository adapter create-not-exists and snapshot privacy

limitations: No real CloudBase transaction, permission/ACL, index, conflict, or failure-recovery behavior was executed against a deployed environment.
Local SDK source compatibility and serial memory/adapter regressions do not constitute production CloudBase transaction acceptance.
The reviewed new source remains unpublished; no deployment or production mutation was performed.
No credentials, environment-secret files, cookies, or keychain data were inspected; no optional lint, build, simulator, installation, or SDK initialization was run.
